references.text: As high priest, Aaron had to offer sacrifices for his own sins before he could offer sacrifices for the people, as prescribed for the sin offering.
On the Day of Atonement, Aaron first had to make atonement for himself and his household before he could make atonement for the people.
The high priest was required to make atonement both for himself and for the people, just as Moses commands Aaron here.
The consecration of Aaron and his sons to the priesthood, which serves as the background for this command.
The Lord had commanded the consecration ceremony leading up to this day when Aaron was to begin his priestly service.
The letter to the Hebrews explains that every high priest must offer sacrifices both for his own sins and for the sins of the people.
Unlike the Levitical high priests who first had to offer sacrifices for their own sins, Jesus did not need to do this.
The high priest entered the Most Holy Place with blood for himself and for the sins of the people.
Atonement (כפר) through the laying on of hands and sacrifice is central to the sacrificial service.
